# Use Le Chat to compare two job offers side‑by‑side in plain English  

**Hook:** By the end of this guide you’ll be able to paste the key points of two employment contracts into Le Chat and receive a tidy, easy‑to‑understand table that highlights the differences—no legal jargon required. This is for anyone who’s juggling two offers and wants confidence before signing.

## Before you start  
- A free (or paid) Mistral account so you can log into Le Chat.  
- Access to the two job offers – either as PDF files you can copy from, or as plain‑text emails.  
- A computer or smartphone with an internet browser.  
- About 10 minutes total – the guide walks you through each click and prompt.

## Step 1 — Open Le Chat and start a new conversation  
Open your web browser, go to the Le Chat web page, and sign in with your Mistral credentials. You’ll see a clean white chat window with a text box at the bottom and a “New chat” button near the top‑right. Click the “New chat” button; a fresh conversation pane slides in, ready for you to type. If the button is labelled differently on your device, look for a plus‑sign icon or a label like “Start new chat”. 💬 Example: *“Hello Le Chat, I need help comparing two job offers.”* You'll know it worked when the chat area shows “New conversation started” or a greeting from the assistant.

## Step 2 — Gather the key points from each offer and copy them as plain text  
Open the first job offer in your email or PDF viewer, then select the most important sections – typically salary, bonuses, work hours, leave entitlements, and notice period. Copy the selected text (Ctrl +C on a computer, long‑press → Copy on a phone). Repeat the same for the second offer, keeping the two chunks separate on your clipboard. On the Le Chat screen you’ll see the empty text box ready for a prompt. If you cannot copy from a PDF, use a PDF‑to‑text converter or type the details manually. 💬 Example: *“Offer A: €70,000 base salary; 15 days annual leave; 1 month notice. Offer B: €68,000 base salary; 20 days annual leave; 2 weeks notice.”* You'll know it worked when the copied text appears in the box after you paste (Ctrl + V).

## Step 3 — Ask Le Chat to create a side‑by‑side comparison in plain English  
With the two offer snippets pasted into the text box, type a clear instruction: *“Please put the details of Offer A and Offer B into a side‑by‑side table and explain the differences in plain English, avoiding legal jargon.”* Press Enter or tap the send icon. Le Chat will start typing a response that usually begins with a markdown‑style table and then bullet points summarising the contrast. If the assistant replies with a single paragraph instead of a table, simply add “Show it as a table” to the prompt. 💬 Example: *“Compare these offers side‑by‑side and list the pros and cons of each in simple language.”* You'll know it worked when you see a two‑column table with headings like “Offer A” and “Offer B” and simple sentences underneath.

## Step 4 — Review the table and ask for clarification if anything looks unclear  
Look at the table Le Chat has generated. Each row should correspond to a contract element (salary, leave, notice, etc.) and each column should contain the figure from the respective offer. If a row is missing (for example, “bonus”), type a follow‑up such as *“Add a row for bonus details for both offers.”* The assistant will update the table accordingly. On some devices the table may appear as plain text rather than a rendered grid; if you see vertical bars (“|”) and dashes (“‑”) instead of a visual grid, that’s still the correct markdown format. 💬 Example: *“Can you explain the impact of the different notice periods in everyday terms?”* You'll know it worked when the assistant adds the requested row or provides a short, jargon‑free explanation beneath the table.

## Step 5 — Save or copy the comparison for later decision‑making  
When the table looks complete, click the three‑dot menu (or right‑click) on the response and choose “Copy message” or “Download as text” depending on your browser. Paste the copied result into a notes app, email to yourself, or print it out. If the copy option isn’t visible, you can manually select the whole response and press Ctrl +C. 💬 Example: *No extra prompt needed – just use the copy command.* You'll know it worked when the entire table appears in your notes or email, ready for you to review side‑by‑side with a coffee.

## Common mistakes  
- **Copying the entire PDF instead of the key points** – the assistant may get overwhelmed. Fix: only copy salary, benefits, leave, and notice details.  
- **Using legal‑sounding wording in the prompt** – Le Chat might mirror that jargon. Fix: ask explicitly for “plain English” or “simple language”.  
- **Forgetting to ask for a table** – you may receive a paragraph of text. Fix: add “show it as a table” or “format as a two‑column chart” in a follow‑up prompt.

## What this means for you  
- **In everyday life:** You can instantly see which offer gives you more vacation days or a higher take‑home pay, without needing a lawyer.  
- **For your business or work:** HR professionals can use the same approach to benchmark internal promotions against external market offers.  
- **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to copy the salary and leave details from one offer and ask Le Chat for a quick plain‑English summary.

## Try it now  
Open Le Chat, paste the salary and leave figures from one of your current job offers, and type: *“Summarise these numbers in simple language.”* In under two minutes you’ll see how Le Chat turns raw numbers into an easy‑to‑understand sentence.
